milestone.title: raul Autopilot lane — live status graph + multi-milestone queue rendering (manual refresh only)

intent.outcome: The Autopilot lane renders a live status graph (per-pane: pane ID, role, last notify, last verifier verdict, cycle count) and a multi-milestone queue view when the active session has more than one milestone; manual `r` refreshes against `mp autopilot session show` and `mp autopilot-control status`.

problem.description: Once a session is running, the raul user needs visibility into what is happening in each pane of the herdr workspace — without leaving the raul window to inspect herdr panes directly. The status graph subscribes (via manual refresh) to the session.json + control-plane state and renders it. Cycle-flow events (C3: WaitingRunner → Reviewing → Deciding, etc.) drive which fields are highlighted. The multi-milestone queue view handles the locked decision that autopilot supports single-milestone OR queue mode (the same pane-set reused across milestones).

in_scope: Per-pane row in the status graph: human-readable tab label (Orchestrator / Runner / Reviewer), pane ID (small caps), role skill name, current stage from session.json (Dispatching / WaitingRunner / Reviewing / Deciding / AwaitingUser — from C3), last notify (role, cycle number, AC pass count), last verifier verdict (`Pass` / `Cycle-next` / `Ship-with-backlog` / `Escalate`), cycle counter.
Multi-milestone queue view: when the session has more than one milestone, render an ordered queue with per-milestone state (current stage, cycle, last verdict). Highlight the active milestone.

Manual refresh: `r` re-reads `mp autopilot session show <id>` and `mp autopilot-control status` via the existing M178 adapter pattern (W179 S4 — `run_preflight` is the predecessor); render is updated from the result.

Verdict / violation surfacing: when C2's verifier emits a typed `Violation`, the status graph shows a 'role violation' badge on the offending pane with the violation name (no detail-dump; click to expand).
out_of_scope: Auto-refresh polling — E (this milestone ships with manual `r` only).
Steering or pause/cancel controls — separate small track, not in this redesign.

acceptance_criteria.description: Per-milestone detail view: pressing Enter on a milestone row expands an inline detail panel showing (a) cycle-flow timeline (per-cycle blocks for done cycles with runner/reviewer/verifier/decision events; active cycle highlighted with cycle-stage, next-action via C3's predict_next_action, drifted seconds, cycle-cap counter); (b) findings block (open count + recently fixed list); (c) rolling history window (last 10 events from session.json queue[i] and activity.json). Tested with golden-file fixtures pinning each field's rendering against a sample session state.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: User-facing recovery controls on the Autopilot lane (per the log's untested list: 'pause / cancel / steer from raul'): (a) **Pause** (`<space>` from the autopilot lane or `Ctrl-P`): orchestrator-pane halts dispatching on the next cycle boundary without teardown — the session stays alive, lanes can finish their current work, no new cycle is dispatched. (b) **Cancel** (`<x>` from the autopilot lane, with confirmation prompt): orchestrator emits a typed `cancel` message to all lane panes; reviewer cleans up its own session-bound notes; session transitions to terminal `cancelled` state and remains in session.json for the history view. (c) **Steer** (`<:` from the autopilot lane opens a small text buffer; user types a message, `<Enter>` sends it via `herdr agent prompt <lane-pane-id> "..."` to a targeted lane — useful for one-off course-correction without restarting a cycle). Each control is exercised in tests; pause + cancel are reversible (re-running the lane resumes), steer is fire-and-forget.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Per-AC visualization: in the per-milestone detail view, below the cycle-flow timeline, render an `ACs (passed / total)` row-by-row breakdown sourced from session.json `queue[i].ac_pass_fail`. Each row shows AC id + description (truncated) + status (passed / failed / pending) + the stamped evidence string. Failed ACs are visually distinct (red marker); pending ACs are neutral. The list scrolls if it overflows the panel. Golden-file tests cover the three status paths and overflow scrolling.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Active-session telemetry aggregates: in the detail view, alongside `drifted` (time-since-last-state-change for the active stage), render cross-milestone aggregates — total time-in-active-stage across all three panes, attempts-per-stage (how many times each cycle stage has been entered across the queue), per-AC pass/fail counts across milestones. Aggregates are computed from session.json state on each refresh; they reset on session start. Golden-file tests cover a synthetic session with one shipped milestone + one in-flight + one pending milestone.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

design_decisions.choice: Manual `r` calls both `mp autopilot session show <id>` (for queued milestones + persisted overrides) and `mp autopilot-control status` (for live pane state).
design_decisions.rationale: Two sources cover both persistent and live state, matching the dual-source pattern in M179 S4 (`mp watch --dry-run` + M178 status).

design_decisions.choice: Badge + click-to-expand rather than always showing detail.
design_decisions.rationale: Detail is verbose; the badge highlights the lane needs attention without crowding the at-a-glance view.

steps.action: Implement the per-milestone detail panel in crates/raul/src/tui/autopilot.rs. Enter on a milestone row expands the panel; second Enter collapses. Renders the cycle-flow timeline by reading queue[i] from session.json (refetched on each r press or auto-refresh tick); renders next-action via a stub that calls C3's predict_next_action once it lands in M213; renders drifted seconds from poller's snapshot diff (M217); renders cycle-cap from session.json; renders findings from milestone JSON via mp reviews finding list; renders history window from activity.json tail. Golden-file tests pin each field's rendering.

steps.action: Implement pause/cancel/steer controls on the autopilot lane in crates/raul/src/tui/autopilot.rs. Each control: pause sets a flag in session.json (`session.controls.paused: true`); orchestrator's cycle flow checks this on every cycle boundary. Cancel sends a typed `cancel` shell command to each lane pane and transitions session.status to `cancelled`. Steer opens a small text-input buffer; on Enter the buffer's text becomes `herdr agent prompt <target-pane-id> "<text>"`. Each control has golden-file tests.

steps.action: Implement active-session telemetry computation in `crates/raul/src/tui/autopilot.rs`. Aggregates pull from session.json at refresh tick: (a) time-in-active-stage = sum of (now - last_state_change_at) for each pane in Working/Reviewing/Deciding; (b) attempts-per-stage = count of cycle-flow transitions per Dispatching/WaitingRunner/Reviewing/Deciding/AwaitingUser state across the queue; (c) per-AC pass/fail counts = sum of status from queue[*].ac_pass_fail. Render as a labeled key-value block in the detail panel above the cycle-flow timeline.
